title: How do we add tenths and hundredths place by place?
description: Two lengths in units, tenths and hundredths are added place by place, with a full place carried to the next. The carrying is compared with adding four hundred eighty three and two hundred sixty eight. Keeko stops before carrying.
teaching_notes: One idea: add each place, then carry when a place holds ten or more, exactly as in whole numbers. Watch for students who leave twelve hundredths as it is.

source: Add 15 3/10 4/100 and 2 6/10 8/100 by adding place by place, and compare with the addition 483 + 268.
video_script.why: The child can write and compare tenths and hundredths and now adds two such numbers, carrying between places.
video_script.substitution: Add units, tenths and hundredths separately, then carry ten of a small place into one of the next bigger place.
video_script.anchor: Two lengths, 15 3/10 4/100 and 2 6/10 8/100, written in columns of units, tenths and hundredths
video_script.wrong_answer: seventeen and nine tenths and twelve hundredths
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko adds each place and stops, leaving 12 hundredths, but 12 hundredths is 1 tenth and 2 hundredths, so the carrying is not finished.
video_script.payoff_line: The sum is eighteen units and two hundredths
never_show: 12 hundredths left uncarried in the final answer
maths_rules: 12 hundredths = 1 tenth + 2 hundredths, so the tenths are 9 + 1 = 10.
10 tenths = 1 unit, so the units are 17 + 1 = 18, leaving 2 hundredths: 18 2/100.
483 + 268: ones 3 + 8 = 11, carry 1 ten; tens 80 + 60 + 10 = 150, carry 1 hundred. Same carrying with different places.
Slip: 17 9/10 12/100 is not finished, because 12 hundredths holds a tenth.
video_script.design: One idea: add each place, then carry when a place holds ten. Assumes the child can write units, tenths and hundredths. Wrong idea: leave twelve hundredths as it is. The columns stay on the board and the comparison with whole numbers comes last.

marks.book: the title card arrives: From your book
marks.two: the two lengths appear one under the other in columns

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Two lengths are written in units, tenths, and hundredths.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What is their sum, and how does it compare with adding whole numbers?

beats.on_screen: the two lengths stay on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: ten small blocks join into one bigger block; hundredths into a tenth, tenths into a unit

marks.ten: ten hundredth blocks join into one tenth block
marks.unit: ten tenth blocks join into one unit block

narration: <bookmark mark='ten'/>Ten hundredths join to make one tenth.
<bookmark mark='unit'/>Ten tenths join to make one unit. A full place always moves to the next place.

marks.given: the two lengths are written in columns

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, fifteen units, three tenths, and four hundredths. And two units, six tenths, and eight hundredths.

beats.on_screen: To find: the sum, adding place by place

marks.find: the words the sum are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the sum by adding place by place.

marks.one: the three columns are added from the units to the hundredths, each total written under its column

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, add each place. The units add to seventeen, the tenths add to nine, and the hundredths add to twelve.

marks.two: 12 hundredths splits into 1 tenth and 2 hundredths
marks.carry: the 1 tenth moves into the tenths column, which becomes 10

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, carry from the hundredths. Twelve hundredths is one tenth and two hundredths.
<bookmark mark='carry'/>The tenth moves over, so the tenths become nine and one, which is ten.

beats.on_screen: 10 tenths = 1 unit; units: 17 + 1 = 18; 2 hundredths are left

marks.three: 10 tenths turns into 1 unit and moves into the units column
marks.left: 2 hundredths stay in the hundredths column

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step three, carry from the tenths. Ten tenths make one unit, so the units become seventeen and one, which is eighteen.
<bookmark mark='left'/>No tenths are left, and two hundredths stay.

beats.on_screen: 483 + 268: ones 3 + 8 = 11, carry 1 ten; tens 8 tens + 6 tens + 1 ten = 15 tens, carry 1 hundred

marks.carry: the carries are shown with arrows from ones to tens and from tens to hundreds

narration: <bookmark mark='four'/>Step four, compare with four hundred eighty three plus two hundred sixty eight. The ones add to eleven, so one ten is carried.
<bookmark mark='carry'/>Then the tens make fifteen tens, so one hundred is carried. It is the same carrying with different places.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The sum is eighteen units and two hundredths.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 17 9/10 12/100; the 12 hundredths column splits into 1 tenth and 2 hundredths; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.fix: the bubble is struck through and 12 hundredths splits into 1 tenth and 2 hundredths

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko says seventeen and nine tenths and twelve hundredths, because each place was added once.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But twelve hundredths holds a full tenth. A place cannot keep ten or more, so it must be carried.
